To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel unsupervised knowledge-based WSD system that outperforms the current state of the art by a significant margin on all datasets.
we propose a novel knowledge based WSD method that utilizes the whole document for disambiguing a word.
we propose a knowledge based WSD method that uses the whole document as context and is based on a variant of LDA.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can topic models be leveraged to design a scalable unsupervised knowledge-based WSD system? What is the impact of the proposed method in different WSD tasks? What is the contribution of different components of the model in the overall performance?

the following questions: (i) How can we leverage the information in WordNet and topic models to design a scalable unsupervised knowledge-based WSD system? (ii) What is the performance of the proposed method compared to the state of the arts?

the following questions: How to use topic model to design WSD systems that scale linearly with the size of context? How to utilize the WordNet information in a topic model based WSD system? How to evaluate a WSD system in a principled way?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a new WSD system that is able to disambiguate words without using any labeled training data.
we propose a novel unsupervised word sense disambiguation approach that is based on a variant of Latnet Dirichlet Allocation topic model that scales linearly to the size of the text.
our proposed model is able to outperform the best existing unsupervised knowledge-based WSD method by a large margin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our system is able not only to outperform the previous state of the art WSD systems but also to disambiguate words in the whole document.

we propose a novel WSD system which utilizes the whole document as context, is computationally tractable and outperforms the current state of the art knowledge based WSD systems by a significant margin.
we have developed a WSD system which is scalable to the whole document, outperforms the previous state of the art and is also able to utilize the WordNet information effectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
topic models provide a powerful framework for WSD that can be easily adapted to different datasets.
a simple modification to topic models can result in a significant performance gain in the WSD task.
a simple modification to topic model can result in a scalable unsupervised knowledge base based WSD system that is able to utilize all the words in the context of a word to be classified.
